Airport security transformed by 9/11 attacks, Americans fear domestic threats

Nearly 25 years after the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks, airport security and air travel in the United States have been significantly transformed. These attacks, which occurred almost a quarter-century ago, led to widespread changes in how Americans fly. Concurrently, recent sentiment indicates that Americans now express greater fear of domestic extremists compared to foreign terrorist threats.
